questions.q: What does a For Each construct do in Flow Designer?
options: Runs its defined actions once per item in a list or array, with no scripting required
Runs a condition check exactly once and branches the flow
Deletes every record returned by a Look Up Records step
Pauses the flow until a human approves it
questions.explain: For Each is Flow Designer's native iteration construct, repeating its loop body once per item.

questions.q: Where does a For Each loop's list of items typically come from?
options: It is always typed in manually as a comma-separated list
A data pill representing multiple records, typically the output of a Look Up Records step
A flow variable set to a fixed number
It cannot accept a list -- only single records
questions.explain: A For Each needs a multi-record pill to iterate over, commonly produced by a Look Up Records action.

questions.q: A Request has five approved Requested Items, and a For Each loop contains one Create Record action. How many fulfillment task records does the flow create?
options: Zero, because For Each only evaluates conditions
One, because the loop only runs a single time
Five, because the loop body runs once per item in the list
It depends on an If/Else being present
questions.explain: The loop body runs once per item in the list, so five Requested Items produce five separate Create Record executions.

questions.q: What does Flow Designer expose on each pass through a For Each loop?
options: A pill representing the current item in that iteration, referenceable like any other data pill
A full copy of the entire original list
Nothing -- items inside the loop can't be referenced individually
Only the first item in the list, repeated every time
questions.explain: Each pass binds a new current-item pill so actions inside the loop can reference that specific item's fields.

questions.q: Can an If/Else condition be placed inside a For Each loop's body?
options: No, For Each and If/Else can never be combined in the same flow
Yes, and it evaluates freshly for each item on every pass through the loop
Only if the loop has exactly one item
Only inside a subflow, never inside a flow
questions.explain: For Each and If/Else can nest together -- the condition is re-evaluated against each current item on every iteration.
